title: Commands
body: `docc init` creates `docc.json`, `docs/schemas/page.json` and `docs/src/index.json` (kind page) if they do not exist and builds `docs/out`, so the first check is green. The configuration it writes has `maxWarnings` 0, so a warning such as a stale link (DOC209) fails `docc check`, and it adds the single-file builds (`docs/out.md`, `docs/out.html`, `docs/out-full*`) to `.gitignore`. In a git repository without a pre-commit hook it also writes `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, which runs `docc check`, so a commit with invalid documentation is refused; an existing hook is never touched.
`docc validate` checks the sources and prints the diagnostics. It changes no files.

`docc build` writes the Markdown into `docs/out`, removes the files it generated earlier that no source produces any more (pages with the GENERATED mark, copies of images, file manager junk) and updates `docc.lock`. When the folder holds any other file it refuses with exit code 2, writes and deletes nothing and lists those files: links that are not in the lock are recorded as confirmed, links that are gone are dropped. When the sources have errors of the groups 1xx or 2xx it writes nothing and exits with code 1. With the flag full it writes the audit build into `docs/out-full` and leaves `docs/out` alone.

The flags single and html add one file next to the folder, each can be combined with full: `docc build --single` writes all pages into one Markdown file (`docs/out.md`) and `docc build --html` into one self-contained HTML application (`docs/out.html`) to read and comment on: a timeline of the saved versions with the edits drawn in the text, and comments ([[rendering]]). The folder of pages is built as before. Once made, such a file is rebuilt by every later `docc build`, with or without the flag, so a stale file is never sent, if docc wrote it; a file of another origin is left alone with a message on stderr, and only the flag replaces it. A bad `changesSince` stops only the HTML file: the diagnostics are still printed and the exit code is 2. These files are for reading, are not committed and are not checked by `docc check`. With full they are `docs/out-full.md` and `docs/out-full.html`.

`docc compile --format json` is for a program that shows the pages itself, such as Docspace. It prints one JSON object on one line and writes nothing: no `docs/out`, no `docc.lock`. The object holds `$schema` (the version of its shape), `ok`, the `summary` and the full list of `diagnostics` as validate reports them, the `project` (title, lang, branding), the `tree` and the `pages` a reader sees, without hidden documents and notes. A page has its id, its path below src, title, kind, status, tags, parent, breadcrumbs, the one-line fields of the property list, its `sections` (the headings of fields and `$sections`, with the anchor that links use as id) and its `blocks`: JSON Pointer, source text, HTML (the same as in the HTML file) and the section the block stands under. The object is printed in every case: with errors of the groups 1xx or 2xx the tree and the pages are empty, and a failure (a bad `docc.json`, an unknown revision) is one diagnostic of code `config`, `usage` or `error` with exit code 2. The exit code is that of validate. `--rev` compiles the tree of a Git revision (a commit, branch or tag) without a checkout: every file of the project comes from that revision, read with `git ls-tree` and `git cat-file --batch`, so includes and links resolve in it and the positions of the diagnostics are those of its files. In a bare repository `--config docs/docc.json` names the project folder. `docc schema compile` prints the JSON Schema of the object.

`docc check` is read-only and made for CI. It runs validate, then compares `docs/out` with what the sources produce (DOC501) and `docc.lock` with the links in the sources (DOC503). With errors of the groups 1xx or 2xx the comparison is skipped.

`docc ack` takes document ids, link targets or code files and sets the stored hashes in `docc.lock` to the current ones for every changed line whose source or target is the argument, or whose target lies in the document with that id. Lines that did not change are left alone. It prints each link it confirmed (`confirmed source -> target`; in JSON a `links` list) and the total, so the reader sees which sources were confirmed. It is run after a person has checked every source flagged by DOC209 or DOC402. `docc ack --all` confirms every changed link.

`docc update` replaces the running binary with a release from GitHub. It reads `checksums.txt` of the release, picks the archive for this system, refuses it when the SHA-256 differs and only then swaps the file. The flag check only reports whether a newer release exists (exit code 1: there is one), the flag version takes a given tag. A development build without a release version refuses to update. The variable DOCC_BASE_URL replaces the releases address, `install.sh` and `install.ps1` read it too.

`docc comments` handles the comments that come from the HTML file as copied text or as a downloaded file. `docc comments import <file>` (`-` reads the copied text from standard input) adds them to `docc.comments.json` in the project root as not processed, skips a comment already there (same id) and attaches a comment whose block moved to the block with the quoted text, and an answer to a form field to the field with its id; the file belongs in git, so the import is part of the history. Without a subcommand it lists the comments not processed yet with the quoted block and its current text (unchanged, moved, changed, removed; an answer says which form field it answers, and changed there means the question was rewritten after it), so an agent can work through them with a person; `--all` lists every comment. `docc comments import --internal` marks internal comments, which stay out of the HTML file. `docc comments done <id>` marks comments as processed, `--reply "text"` stores the answer the reader sees under the comment in the next HTML file, and `docc comments rm <id>` deletes them; an id may be shortened to a unique prefix.
Every command accepts --help and prints its flags with an example. The global flags may stand before or after the command. `docc init` ends with a Next block of steps.

`docc explain` takes a code in any case (doc209), a name (style/hedging) or a group (graph, style): a rule with an example, or for a group the list of its rules. `docc rules` lists the rules with their effective levels; `docc schema document`, `docc schema config` and `docc schema compile` print the JSON Schemas.
The settings are in [[config]] and the generated pages in [[rendering]].
flags: format text or json, config, max-diagnostics (default 20, errors first, applies to both formats, 0 means no limit, negative values are rejected), max-warnings.
exit_codes: 1: errors, or more effective warnings than the limit.

2: wrong usage or configuration, including a missing source folder or a kind schema that does not load. The message goes to stderr; with `--format json` it is the usual report (`summary`, `diagnostics`) with diagnostics of code `config`, `usage` or `error`, and every error of `docc.json` is listed at once.
